name: Owner Check After CPI
description: Trusting an account's data after a cross-program invocation without re-establishing who owns it. A CPI can reassign an account to another program, and Anchor's reload() re-deserializes the bytes without re-checking the owner - so the data read afterwards can be entirely attacker-controlled. An ownership check made before the CPI proves nothing about the account after it. The fix re-checks the owner between the CPI and the next use of the account's data.

name: Unvalidated Instruction Introspection
description: Reading a neighbouring instruction through the instructions sysvar and trusting its contents without checking which program it belongs to. Any account can put any instruction at any index of a transaction, so an introspected instruction proves nothing until its program id is established - making it look like the expected one is the attack, not an obstacle to it. The fix compares the loaded instruction's program_id against the program that is supposed to have produced it.

name: Mint Configuration Unvalidated
description: Accepting a token mint and pricing amounts in its raw units without checking the mint's decimals. Two mints sharing a symbol and differing in decimals value the same integer amount orders of magnitude apart, so a protocol that never checks credits whatever the caller's mint claims. The fix compares the mint's decimals against the value the protocol prices in.
